requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.

rationale:
I found no gap in `requirements.authoring.reporting`. I read the code and tests below and did not run the tests.

**Where the code is**
- The `{impl}` is `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, in the `Command::Author` arm.
- It reaches the batch reporting in `src/authoring/progress.rs#impl[BatchProgress]`, through `AuthoringOptions.verbose` and `BatchProgress::new(options.verbose)`.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Suppress per-subject `true` lines and show each `false` subject and outcome on stderr, on terminals and redirected output.**
  - In batch, `BatchProgress::completed` prints nothing for `Judgment::True`. For `False` it prints `<subject>: false (usage: …)` through `println`.
  - `println` uses `bar.println` on a terminal and `eprintln!` otherwise, so both cases go to stderr.
  - In single-subject mode, `main` does `eprintln!("{}: false", outcome.subject)` for a false judgment and prints nothing for a true one.
- **Keep progress counters and completion summaries.**
  - `BatchProgress::refresh` and `finish` keep the counters.
  - `main` prints the `N authored; … failed; policy …` summary on stdout.
- **Keep FIXME notices and authoring errors visible.**
  - `BatchProgress::completed` prints `<subject>: FIXME`, and `failed` prints `label: error`.
  - In single-subject mode, `main` appends ` — FIXME` to the summary line and returns errors as `Err`.
- **Single-subject mode keeps subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage metadata.** `main` prints `subject: backend / model; policy …`, then `Evidence: <path|stdout>` and `Usage: <path>`.
- **`-v` and `--verbose` also show each false rationale on stderr, and rationales are omitted by default, in single and batch modes.**
  - Batch appends `assessment.rationale` only when `self.verbose` is set, for false judgments only.
  - Single-subject mode does the same in `main`.
- **Do not print true rationales or append input snapshots.** Only the recorded `rationale` string is printed, and only for false judgments.
- **Reporting uses the completed result without extra inference.** Both paths read `outcome.determination` and `outcome.rationale` from the finished assessment.
- **In `--stdout` mode, stdout is only the evidence JSON and all diagnostics go to stderr.** The single-subject summary and the false and rationale lines go through `eprintln!` when `evidence_path` is `None`.
- **Verbosity does not change persistence, validation or exit status.** `verbose` is read only in the printing code (`BatchProgress::new` and `completed`, and `main`).

**Tests**
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose]` covers batch, redirected, with and without `--verbose`. It asserts that true lines are absent, that the false line appears, and that the rationale appears only with `-v`. It also asserts that no source snapshot or true rationale appears, that FIXME and errors are shown, and that the stdout summary and non-zero exit are unchanged.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors]` covers the terminal path: counters, the completion summary, and the false, FIXME and error lines.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress]` covers a verbose rationale above the terminal progress display.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure]` covers error visibility and the non-zero exit.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers single-subject mode with `-v` and `--verbose`. It asserts the false line and rationale only for false, no true line, no source text, and that `Evidence:` and `Usage:` are present.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` covers `--stdout` for true, false and FIXME, with and without verbose. It asserts that stdout is only JSON and that stderr holds the backend/model line, `Evidence: stdout`, the usage path and the false line. It also asserts that the rationale appears only for verbose false, and that evidence persistence is unchanged.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` asserts that the false line is on stderr, not stdout, and that the rationale is absent by default.

rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded

{cite}`requirements.authoring.invocation` {cite}`requirements.authoring.batch`
:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
A denied mandatory input MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption arrives MUST NOT write it. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
